[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Seq2Seq Models and Attention Mechanisms"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) Architecture"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) models are a specialized class of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) designed to map an input sequence of variable length to an output sequence of variable length. This architecture is fundamental for tasks such as neural machine translation, text summarization, and speech recognition."},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Encoder: Processes the input sequence token by token and compresses the entire semantic meaning into a fixed-size context vector."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Decoder: Takes the context vector and generates the target sequence token by token autoregressively."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"The Bottleneck Problem in Traditional Seq2Seq Models"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Standard Seq2Seq architectures suffer from a critical limitation known as the information bottleneck. Because the encoder must compress all information from the input sequence into a single, fixed-length context vector, the model struggles to retain long-range dependencies. As the input sequence grows longer, the vector loses crucial details, leading to degraded performance."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"The Attention Mechanism Solution"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Attention Mechanism was introduced to resolve the bottleneck problem. Instead of forcing the decoder to rely solely on a single context vector, attention allows the decoder to look back at all encoder hidden states for every step of decoding. It assigns varying weights (attention scores) to different parts of the input sequence, effectively focusing on the most relevant information dynamically."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"PyTorch Implementation of Attention"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a simplified implementation of an additive attention layer in PyTorch, demonstrating how context vectors are computed dynamically using encoder hidden states and the current decoder hidden state."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Attention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, hidden_dim):
        super(Attention, self).__init__()
        self.attn = nn.Linear(hidden_dim * 2, hidden_dim)
        self.v = nn.Parameter(torch.rand(hidden_dim))

    def forward(self, hidden, encoder_outputs):
        # hidden: [batch_size, hidden_dim]
        # encoder_outputs: [batch_size, seq_len, hidden_dim]
        seq_len = encoder_outputs.shape[1]
        
        hidden = hidden.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, seq_len, 1)
        energy = torch.tanh(self.attn(torch.cat((hidden, encoder_outputs), dim=2)))
        energy = energy.permute(0, 2, 1)
        
        v = self.v.repeat(encoder_outputs.shape[0], 1).unsqueeze(1)
        attention_scores = torch.bmm(v, energy).squeeze(1)
        
        return torch.softmax(attention_scores, dim=1)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Seq2Seq models combined with attention mechanisms revolutionized Natural Language Processing by eliminating the fixed-size context bottleneck. This laid the foundation for modern Transformer architectures, which rely entirely on self-attention mechanisms to process sequences in parallel."}]
